title: "Nearest Neighbors"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## Overview

This example demonstrates k-nearest neighbors and radius neighbors searches using the `aoclda` package.

```{r library}
library(aoclda)
```

## Define Data

```{r data}
x_train <- matrix(
   c(
      -1, -2, -3, 1, 2, 3,
      -1, -1, -2, 3, 5, -1,
      2, 3, -1, 1, 1, 2
   ),
   nrow = 6, ncol = 3
)

x_test <- matrix(
   c(
      -2, -1, 2,
      2, -2, 1,
      3, -1, -3
   ),
   nrow = 3, ncol = 3
)

nn <- nearest_neighbors$new()
nn$fit(x_train)
```

## k-Nearest Neighbors

```{r knn}
result <- nn$kneighbors(x_test, n_neighbors = 3, return_distance = TRUE)
k_ind <- result$indices
k_dist <- result$distances

cat("Indices of the nearest neighbors:\n")
print(k_ind)

cat("\nCorresponding distances of the nearest neighbors:\n")
print(k_dist)
```

## Radius Neighbors

```{r radius}
result_r <- nn$radius_neighbors(x_test,
   radius = 2.0,
   return_distance = TRUE, sort_results = FALSE
)

cat("Indices of the radius neighbors:\n")
print(lapply(result_r, function(e) e$indices))

cat("\nCorresponding distances of the radius neighbors:\n")
print(lapply(result_r, function(e) e$distances))
```
